To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including

[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly

disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,

must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's Draft Against Buyer Playbook

**Preliminary point:** The Seller's cover note and "Key Negotiated Positions" describe these terms as negotiated. They are not. Nothing in the file shows that Amelia Frost has approved any Seller position, so none should be treated as agreed. The Seller's 20% / AUD 4.8m cap is our conditional fallback, and it is available only with her prior written authority identifying the draft. That authority has not been given. The 18-month claims period is likewise a fallback needing her written approval.

This review is a playbook comparison, not a formal legal opinion. NSW law points and drafting should be confirmed by the responsible lawyer.

---

## 1. Material issues, in priority order

### (a) The liability regime is cumulatively destructive
Several Seller positions compound each other, so they must be assessed together, not one at a time:

- **Cap:** 20% / AUD 4.8m against our 25% / AUD 6m.
- **De minimis:** AUD 25,000 against our AUD 5,000.
- **Basket:** AUD 250,000, excess-only, against our AUD 50,000 tipping basket.
- **Time limit:** 18 months against our 24 months.
- **Knowledge exclusion, reliance and disclosure** all narrow recovery further (see below).

**Illustration:** Suppose claims with a combined value of AUD 240,000, each above the de minimis. Under the Seller's draft, aggregate claims do not exceed the AUD 250,000 basket, so nothing is recoverable. Under our playbook, the basket is exceeded and the seller is liable from the first dollar, so the full AUD 240,000 is recoverable, well within the cap.

**Reasoning:** The Seller's package makes the general warranties close to illusory for claims of the size most likely to arise in a business of this kind. This is the single most important point to make back.

### (b) Fundamental/Title claims pulled into the general regime
The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity." Our playbook requires a separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.

**Reasoning:** Title is the buyer's core protection. Capping it at 20% and 18 months would leave us with no real recourse if the seller's title to the shares turns out to be defective. This is a non-negotiable departure. Combined with the "limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" wording, it is effectively a hidden general-regime override, which the playbook prohibits.

### (c) Fraud carve-out is absent or at risk
The Seller applies the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature" (clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5). There is no fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate-misconduct carve-out in the Seller's summary.

**Reasoning:** Our playbook requires the carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and says no one may waive it. The drafting must be checked to confirm it is present, not just implied. Non-reliance language in particular must not be able to bar a fraud claim.

### (d) Disclosure and buyer knowledge
- **Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2** disclose the entire data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records. Our playbook rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Clause 8.3** bars claims in respect of anything the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge" of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. The playbook requires blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions to be deleted.

**Reasoning:** Under this drafting, the buyer's own diligence would waive its claims. The disclosure letter also cross-refers to DD-002 to DD-012, so its general disclosure would extend to the same documents on which the Seller relies for title (DD-012). The disclosure should be limited to specific, fairly disclosed matters. The knowledge clause should be deleted, or at most allow a qualifier naming seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

Disclosure Letter 1.4 says nothing admits "that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required." This is a non-admission, which is acceptable as a drafting protection. But it must not be read as a Seller statement that these items are not required, and we should not rely on it as a factual position.

### (e) Bluefen consent (about 30% of FY26 revenue)
The Seller proposes reasonable endeavours and treating consent as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." The Disclosure Letter (item 2) confirms no final written consent or evidence of satisfied conditions exists.

**Reasoning:** Our playbook requires an effective consent and evidence that its conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied before Completion. Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours are insufficient for a material customer consent. This should be a condition precedent, not a post-signing aspiration.

### (f) Riverlark facility (about AUD 3.2m)
The Seller will provide a release "following Completion." The Disclosure Letter (item 3) confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge of security is included. The funds flow does not mention Riverlark.

**Reasoning:** This is a debt-like item in a debt-free/cash-free deal. Our playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. Leaving a AUD 3.2m secured facility open after Completion is a serious exposure.

### (g) Employee bonuses (AUD 420,000)
The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure item 5 notes that payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are not addressed.

**Reasoning:** Our playbook requires the bonuses to be either a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, including triggered on-costs. Silent exclusion from the funds flow is not acceptable. Even if the Seller says it will fund these, that must be documented, not left to informal assurances.

### (h) Ironquay IP
The Seller calls the indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment "adequate." Disclosure item 4 notes that DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 project materials on payment of every SOW3 fee, that AUD 180,000 appears open, and that no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

**Reasoning:** Our playbook requires the indemnity to be broadened, while preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 figure is not independently verified, so we should neither accept nor reject it as the correct amount. The practical protection is to require evidence of payment and a confirmatory assignment before Completion, plus a broader indemnity covering IP ownership and transfer defects.

### (i) Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
The Seller describes this as "a preliminary operational matter... not expected to be material." Disclosure item 6 states the investigation is preliminary, does not confirm a breach, and does not establish access, scope or notification obligations. It refers to possibly around 1,240 records.

**Reasoning:** Our playbook requires log preservation, investigation and regular updates, and assumes no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. The Seller's expectation that the matter is "not material" is not a fact we can accept, and equally we should not overstate the exposure. The right response is a covenant to preserve logs, complete the investigation and provide updates before Completion, with protection that does not presuppose the outcome.

### (j) Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
The Seller calls these ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure item 8 says the material does not show whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Reasoning:** Our playbook requires assessment, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. We should not accept the "ordinary course" characterisation without analysis, but we also should not impose an automatic deduction.

### (k) Tax and IP
The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime." The playbook keeps these open and requires them to be kept separate from the general regime.

**Reasoning:** This is a hidden override. Tax and IP remain open. Our working assumption is that there is no resolution and no unlimited liability agreed.

### (l) Title evidence
The Seller relies on the share register at DD-012 as evidence of title. The Disclosure Letter (item 10) concedes it is the source relied on, not a Buyer verification.

**Reasoning:** Our playbook says DD-012 is an internal, supplied source, not independent proof. We require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. Examples include an ASIC company extract, PPSR and encumbrance searches, executed share transfer documents, and evidence of the seller's authority to sell. Also note the circularity: the Seller relies on a document that its own general disclosure also covers.

### (m) Other open items (not directly covered by the playbook)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Disclosure item 7 identifies a notification obligation but does not say whether landlord consent is needed for the share sale.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Disclosure item 9 identifies an assignment restriction, but does not say that consent is required merely because shares are sold.

**Reasoning:** Neither point is covered by the playbook, so I should not invent a position. The practical step is to obtain a legal analysis of each provision and decide whether a consent or waiver should be a condition or a specific disclosure item.

---

## 2. Summary of recommendations

| # | Area | Seller position | Our position | Action |
|---|------|----------------|--------------|--------|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m | Reject. Restore starting position. |
| 2 | De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. |
| 3 | Basket | AUD 250,000, excess-only | AUD 50,000, tipping | Reject. |
| 4 | Time limit (general) | 18 months | 24 months | Reject. Do not offer 18m without Frost written approval. |
| 5 | Universal limitations | Apply to all Claims | Separate regimes | Reject. No hidden override. |
| 6 | Fundamental/title | Same as general | 100%, 6+ years, outside basket | Reject. |
| 7 | Fraud carve-out | Not evident | Carve-out, non-waivable | Confirm in drafting. |
| 8 | Disclosure | Whole data room, registers | Specific fair disclosure | Reject deemed disclosure. |
| 9 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket exclusion | Delete | Reject. |
| 10 | Bluefen | Endeavours; satisfied on delivery | Effective consent + evidence pre-Completion | Make a CP. |
| 11 | Riverlark | Release post-Completion | Payout and direct repayment; irrevocable undertaking if post-Completion | Require payout letter and funds-flow repayment. |
| 12 | Bonuses (AUD 420k) | Excluded from funds flow | Specific line item or Seller-funded, incl. on-costs | Require funds-flow line item or Seller funding. |
| 13 | Ironquay IP | Adequate as is | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure | Require payment evidence, confirmatory assignment, broader indemnity. |
| 14 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Preserve logs, investigate, update; no assumed outcome | Require covenant and updates. |
| 15 | Sandbar (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | Assess; no automatic deduction | Require assessment. |
| 16 | Tax / IP | Settled under general regime | Open; separate | Reject override. |
| 17 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent evidence | Require ASIC, PPSR and transfer evidence. |
| 18 | Lease / Mossvale | Not addressed | Not in playbook | Obtain legal analysis. |

### Overall recommendation
Return a mark-up that rejects the Seller's "key negotiated positions" as agreed. State clearly that no fallback has been authorised. Table the buyer's playbook positions as the starting point for negotiation. Then prioritise the following for the next round:

1. Restore the separate title regime and the fraud carve-out.
2. Replace the disclosure and knowledge provisions with specific fair disclosure.
3. Make Bluefen consent and Riverlark payout conditions to Completion.
4. Put the AUD 420,000 bonuses and on-costs into the funds flow, or require Seller funding.
5. Restore the general cap, thresholds and time limit to playbook positions.

Any move toward the 20% cap or 18-month period requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the specific draft. That authority has not been given, so none should be offered.
